items.title: ‘I want to make her proud’: My mother, a divorcée, died and I’m her executor. Do I need to file for probate?
items.summary: “The only debts were utility and credit-card bills, which we will pay off.”

items.title: ‘We lived within our means’: I earned $30,000 as a pastor and still retired comfortably. Why don’t you tell people that?
items.summary: “As a country, we have grown dangerously comfortable.”

items.title: A ‘death cross’ is coming for the dollar. Why Trump will be happy.
items.summary: Don’t look now, but there are some technical reasons to believe that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was right when he declared to the financial markets that “I am the house now.”

items.title: Social Security overpaid my 82-year-old mother by $20,000. What else is hiding in her finances?
items.summary: “My mother has a pension, Social Security, investments and a house probably worth over $1 million.”

items.title: My husband and I are in our 50s and have no kids. We have $2 million in IRAs and 401(k)s. Do we really need a will?
items.summary: “We have no debt and own our primary home, a vacation home, as well as my mother’s home in another state.”

items.title: ‘It doesn’t seem fair’: I’m retired and have plenty of money. Why can’t I qualify for a retail credit card?
items.summary: “I draw from my IRA as needed for household repairs, trips and other larger expenses.”

items.title: My friend is terminally ill. Should she sell her rental home and pay $100,000 in capital gains?
items.summary: “Her younger son lives in the condo, but wants to move elsewhere with friends.”

items.title: I’m 77, pay rent and live off Social Security, but I help homeless people. Why are so many people going hungry?
items.summary: “I am a retired senior citizen living check-to-check.”

items.title: Micron could dethrone Nvidia and become the biggest driver of S&P 500 profit growth
items.summary: Micron is increasingly important to the S&P 500, and its earnings report has become “a market event in and of itself.”

items.title: Look closer, and Wall Street’s rally is showing cracks
items.summary: Major stock indexes hovering near records are masking a market straining under elevated oil prices, rising Treasury yields and a Federal Reserve bracing for additional interest-rate hikes.
